character: This is the newest MFT program in the state's private sector and it should be read as such. Benerd College announced it on 31 December 2023 and opened it to students in fall 2024, projecting an inaugural class of "approximately 15 to 20 students." The stated reason is a real one: San Joaquin County has California's thinnest mental-health workforce — six psychiatrists and 16 psychologists per 100,000 residents against state averages of 12 and 44 — and the program lead, associate professor Justin Low, framed it around that shortage. The first cohort, on the published two-year program of study, would have finished in summer 2026. As of this research (August 2026) Pacific has published nothing about graduates, completion rates, BBS registration or licensure outcomes, and there is no student discussion of the program anywhere findable. A prospective student is being asked to commit roughly $77,000 to a program with no track record on the public record at all. That is not a criticism of the teaching; it is a description of the evidence available.

The program cannot support international students: the program page carries the flat statement "This program format cannot support an I-20 for international student visas." That follows from the format — Benerd advertises it as a "Flexible hybrid program" with an "Accelerated course schedule," "whether online or in the classroom," and a hybrid/online-flexible degree cannot meet the in-person course-load rules an F-1 visa requires. The catalog lists the MA in Counseling Psychology as a Stockton Campus program, alongside emphases in Professional Clinical Counseling and Child and Adolescent Counseling.

The question of how a counselling program sits inside an education school has a concrete answer here, and you can read it off the required course list. Benerd College is Pacific's school of education (Gladys L. Benerd Building; Dean Patricia J. Campbell), and the MA sits in a Department of Counseling and School Psychology chaired by the MFT program lead himself. That department is not new — it also runs an EdS in School Psychology, an EdD in Counseling Psychology and a PsyD in Counseling Psychology — so there is a standing doctoral counselling faculty. But the shared course pool is a school-psychology pool, and MFT students take courses written for other people. Consultation Methods, required in Year 2 Fall of the MFT program of study, has this catalog description: "This course prepares school psychologists to provide mental health consultation to school personnel and parents. Various consultation methodologies will be studied with applications particularly appropriate to children in the public school system." Nature and Conditions of Learning, required in the final summer, is a teaching-methods course: "Students study both cognitive and traditional learning theories, their applications to instruction and the development of effective teaching strategies." Those are six of your units. The upside of the same arrangement is that the catalog states "Students who take PsyD courses as part of a MA degree completed at Pacific may count those units towards their PsyD" — a doctoral on-ramp most standalone MFT programs do not have.
orientation: Generalist counselling psychology with a multicultural framing — the two named systemic courses are both titled ‘Theories of Multicultural…’, and the program's stated learning outcome is to "interrogate structures of power from the standpoint of cultural inheritance"

signature.title: Theories of Multicultural Family Therapy and Collaboration
signature.desc: "This course prepares mental health clinicians to assess functioning in and design and implement interventions for couples and families by studying major theories of couples and family therapy. This course also prepares mental health clinicians to help families collaborate with helping institutions to improve the well-being of children."
signature.why: This is the systemic core of the degree and its second half is unusual — ‘collaborate with helping institutions’ is child-welfare and school-system language, not family-therapy-model language. It is a fair signal that the training is aimed at agency and school-adjacent practice rather than private-practice couples work.

signature.title: Theories of Multicultural Couples Therapy
signature.desc: "This course introduces major theories of couples counseling. It prepares mental health clinicians to assess functioning in couples from diverse backgrounds and to design and implement interventions for couples. Students in this course will study evidence-based approaches to couples counseling, legal and ethical considerations in marriage and couples counseling, relationship violence, and separation and divorce."
signature.why: The couples half of the systemic pair, and the only dedicated couples course in the program. Between this and CPSY 328 the entire relational-therapy content of a 62-unit MFT degree is six units — worth weighing against programs that run four or five systemic courses.

signature.title: Consultation Methods
signature.desc: "This course prepares school psychologists to provide mental health consultation to school personnel and parents. Various consultation methodologies will be studied with applications particularly appropriate to children in the public school system."
signature.why: Required in Year 2 Fall of the MFT program of study, and its catalog description does not mention marriage and family therapy at all — it is written for school psychologists. This is the sharpest single illustration of an MFT degree drawing on an education school's existing course pool.

signature.title: Nature and Conditions of Learning
signature.desc: "Students study both cognitive and traditional learning theories, their applications to instruction and the development of effective teaching strategies. In addition, information processing models are explored and their implications for instruction are addressed."
signature.why: A teaching-methods course, required in the final summer term. Combined with Consultation Methods that is six of the program's units spent on instruction and school consultation rather than on clinical practice — the clearest cost of the program's location inside Benerd.

signature.title: Human Sexuality
signature.desc: "This course reviews the basic anatomy, sexual function and response, and challenges and disorders of sexual function. Diagnostic formulations and treatments for the disorders that clinicians are most likely to encounter in clinical practice are also presented."
signature.why: One unit, where most California MFT programs run human sexuality as a full three-unit course. It meets the BBS content area, but if sexuality is central to the practice you want, this is a very thin treatment — and it is scheduled in the last term, after your practicum has finished.

signature.title: Counseling Practicum
signature.units: 1–6 in the catalog; 3 + 3 on the published program of study
signature.desc: The entire catalog description reads: "Counseling Practicum entails the supervised application of psychological procedures in appropriate settings." One sentence.
signature.why: For the course that carries every client hour in the degree, this is the least information any of the California programs in this guide publish. There is no practicum handbook, no hour table, no supervision ratio and no partner-site list on Pacific's public site. Ask for the fieldwork manual before you deposit.

curriculum.note: Two years, six terms, cohort-based, on the Stockton campus, delivered in a flexible hybrid format ("whether online or in the classroom") with an accelerated schedule and two summer terms. Course codes below are as published on the program page (EDUC prefix); the 2026–27 academic catalog carries the same courses under a CPSY prefix, which is the current registrar coding — e.g. EDUC 388 Counseling Practicum is CPSY 394. Units below sum to 62, not the 60 the program's press materials quote.
curriculum.total_units: 62 per the published program of study. The 2026–27 catalog frames the same degree as a 15-unit core plus "Select 46 units of the following" for the Marriage and Family Therapy emphasis (61), against a generic MA minimum of 32 units; Pacific's own tuition table lists the MA in Counseling Psychology at "32–63 units." The 60 figure comes from the 2023 launch announcement.

practicum.starts: Year 2, Fall term — EDUC 388 / CPSY 394 Counseling Practicum, 3 units, repeated for 3 more units in Year 2 Spring. The first full year is classroom only.
practicum.hours: 280 hours of client work, per the university's own launch announcement ("an experiential requirement of 280 hours of patient work"). This figure appears in Pacific's newsroom, not in the catalog, the program page or any published handbook — there is no official hour table.
practicum.clinic: None documented for this program. Pacific operates Counseling and Psychological Services (CAPS), which has held APA accreditation for its doctoral internship since 2011, but that is the university's own student counselling service and its training programme is doctoral-level; no in-house training clinic serving community clients with MA MFT trainees is described anywhere.
practicum.detail: Pacific publishes less about its practicum than any other program in this set, and that is the finding. What is establishable: it starts in the second year, it runs two terms rather than three, and it carries six of the degree's sixty-two units — EDUC 388 in Year 2 Fall and again in Year 2 Spring, three units each, sitting alongside a full three-course academic load in both terms, which is a heavier concurrent load than programs that thin out the second year for fieldwork. The catalog description for the course is a single sentence: "Counseling Practicum entails the supervised application of psychological procedures in appropriate settings." The only hour figure anywhere in Pacific's own materials is in the 2023 launch story, which describes "an experiential requirement of 280 hours of patient work" and says it will be done "with identified agencies" alongside adjunct faculty — phrasing that implies the program maintains relationships with placement sites rather than leaving students to cold-call, but it is a newsroom paraphrase, not a policy, and Pacific has not published a partner-site list, a placement process, an application timeline or an eligibility gate. There is no published relational (couple/family) sub-minimum, which matters because the BBS requires relational hours for LMFT registration and every other program in this set states one. There is no published supervision ratio, no statement of who supervises on site or what their licence must be, no weekly hour expectation, no liability-insurance requirement and no practicum handbook of any kind on the public site. Every one of those is a question to put to the program in writing before depositing, and the absence of answers should weigh more heavily here than it would at a twenty-year-old program, because there is also no cohort of alumni to ask.
practicum.model_evidence: Counseling Practicum entails the supervised application of psychological procedures in appropriate settings.

admissions.cohort_size: "Approximately 15 to 20 students" was the projection for the inaugural fall 2024 class. No enrolment figures have been published since.
admissions.prereqs: "A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 units of college or post-baccalaureate work"; a bachelor's degree from an accredited university; a completed application portfolio including an essay, official transcripts and three letters of recommendation; a program interview; and "Evidence of qualities and character in keeping with the philosophy and standards of this University and Benerd Education Programs." Up to nine semester units may transfer in, but "Not all courses are eligible for transfer credit for the Marriage and Family Therapy and Professional Clinical Counselor programs." Graduation requires a capstone plus "A final oral examination, conducted by program faculty."
admissions.deadline: A 1 June registration deadline for fall entry was reported at launch; no deadline is currently published on the program page.
admissions.gre_evidence: A cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better for the last 60 units of college or post-baccalaureate work

cost.per_unit: $1,244 per unit for the MA in Counseling Psychology, Fall 2026 / Spring 2027
cost.tuition_total: 62 units × $1,244 = $77,128. (Pacific's tuition table lists the program at 32–63 units; the 2023 launch story quoted annual tuition of "approximately $34,000.")
cost.fees: Per term at 9+ units: Wellness Center $300, ASUOP Student Activity Fee $150, Activity & Rec Center Fee $150. Student Health Insurance $2,524, waivable with proof of coverage.

gaps: Whether the program has produced graduates. It opened fall 2024 on a two-year program of study ending in a Year 2 Summer term, so the first cohort would have finished around August 2026. Pacific has published no commencement note, graduate count, completion rate or alumni profile for it, and no BBS or licensure outcome data exists.
Licensure outcomes, BBS associate-registration rates and employment outcomes — none published, and the program is too young for meaningful data to exist yet.
Current enrolment. The only figure anywhere is the pre-launch projection of "approximately 15 to 20 students" for the fall 2024 cohort.

The entire practicum apparatus: who finds the site, when the search starts, the supervision ratio, the supervisor's required licence and tenure, the weekly hour commitment, any relational (couple/family) hour sub-minimum, and any liability-insurance requirement. No practicum or fieldwork handbook is published. The 280-hour figure comes from a university newsroom story, not a policy document.

The exact unit total is stated three different ways in Pacific's own materials — 60 (2023 launch announcement and press coverage), 61 (2026–27 catalog: 15-unit core plus "Select 46 units" for the MFT emphasis), 62 (the term-by-term program of study on the program page), and "32–63 units" (the Benerd graduate tuition table). Nothing on the public site reconciles them.

Course prefixes do not match between sources. The program page's plan of study uses EDUC codes (EDUC 388 Counseling Practicum, EDUC 334 Theories of Multicultural MFT); the 2026–27 academic catalog carries the same courses under CPSY (CPSY 394, CPSY 328). At least one of the two is stale. Course descriptions in this file are the catalog's CPSY entries.

Two courses on the program of study could not be matched confidently to a catalog entry: EDUC 324 Intro to Counseling is listed at 1 unit while the catalog's CPSY 302 Introduction to Counseling is 3 units, and EDUC 393 Advanced Psychotherapeutic Tech appears to correspond to CPSY 322 Advanced Psychotherapeutic Interventions rather than to CPSY 393 Special Topics.

The catalog's Marriage and Family Therapy emphasis course list does not separately include CPSY 335 Child Abuse Assessment and Reporting or CPSY 334 Spousal and Partner Abuse, Detection, and Intervention — both of which do appear in the Professional Clinical Counseling emphasis list. The MFT track instead carries CPSY 333 Abuse and Crisis Intervention for Families. How the BBS child-abuse and partner-abuse content requirements are satisfied is not spelled out.

No student discussion of this program exists on Reddit, Student Doctor Network, GradCafe or elsewhere — which is expected for a program two years old, but leaves an applicant with no independent account of what it is like.

Whether LPCC eligibility can be added. Benerd offers a separate Professional Clinical Counseling emphasis of the same MA, but nothing published says whether an MFT-emphasis student can also earn LPCC eligibility, or at what unit cost. The catalog does say "A single course may be used to fulfill requirements in two or more concentrations, but the units will not count twice."

Accreditation: no COAMFTE or CACREP accreditation is claimed. Pacific's APA accreditation belongs to the CAPS doctoral internship, which is a different thing entirely and should not be read as accreditation of this master's.

corrections.correct: The published two-year program of study totals 62 units (13 + 12 + 6 + 12 + 12 + 7). The 2026–27 catalog describes the same degree as a 15-unit core plus "Select 46 units" for the MFT emphasis (61), and Pacific's tuition table lists the program at "32–63 units." 60 is the round number from the December 2023 launch announcement and should not be used for cost estimates — at $1,244/unit the difference between 60 and 62 is $2,488.

The program page's plan of study uses EDUC course codes; the current 2026–27 academic catalog carries the identical courses under CPSY codes (EDUC 388 Counseling Practicum = CPSY 394; EDUC 334 Theories of Multicultural MFT = CPSY 328; EDUC 338 Consultation Methods = CPSY 340). Anyone citing this program's courses should note which source they took the code from.
Announced 31 December 2023, first cohort enrolled fall 2024, projected inaugural class of approximately 15–20 students. As of August 2026 no graduate, completion or licensure data has been published.

$1,244 per unit for Fall 2026/Spring 2027 — $77,128 for the 62-unit program of study. Plus roughly $600/term in wellness, activity and recreation fees at full-time enrolment, and a waivable $2,524 health-insurance charge.

Correct as stated by the program ("Flexible hybrid program," "whether online or in the classroom," "Accelerated course schedule"), with the important consequence spelled out on the same page: "This program format cannot support an I-20 for international student visas." The catalog places the degree on the Stockton campus.
